summary: iter_20 security audit fixes verified: (1) 41/41 tests pass across the four suites requested (test_realworld_file_shapes 8/8, test_corpus 14/14, test_security_findings 6/6, test_security_audit_iter18 13/13). (2) Sir's real diabetes.csv + dict.docx study package accepted end-to-end via POST /api/sessions then /intake with exit_code=0, both files linked (dataset + dictionary). (3) Decompression-bomb docx (>10 MiB inflated document.xml, ~50 KB archive) is rejected by _read_docx_tables returning '' -- covered by test_read_docx_tables_rejects_oversize_document_xml. (4) Billion-laughs DTD docx is rejected by defusedxml.forbid_dtd=True returning '' -- covered by test_read_docx_tables_refuses_dtd_via_defusedxml. (5) Deterministic replay of the docx reader on Sir's real 12 KB dict.docx returns 2743 chars including all table rows.
critical_code_review_comments: specialists.py:_read_docx_tables correctly enforces both defenses (declared file_size cap AND streamed read cap of _DOCX_XML_MAX_BYTES+1) which handles archives that lie about uncompressed size. Clean defense-in-depth.

defusedxml.ElementTree.fromstring(raw, forbid_dtd=True) is the right primitive; ParseError is caught alongside BadZipFile/ValueError so all malformed inputs degrade to empty string rather than raising into the async agent path.
_read_xls_tables dead-code cleanup done: xlrd fallback removed, contract preserved (returns '' rather than crashing). test_read_xls_tables_handles_xlsx_disguised_as_xls locks that contract.

Minor observation (non-blocking): the SEC-001 cap of 10 MiB is documented inline; suggest also asserting the max at a shared config-level constant if intake ever needs the same ceiling elsewhere, but not required now.
